Class MapPolygonItem

java.lang.Object
edu.cnu.mdi.item.AItem
edu.cnu.mdi.mapping.item.AMapItem
edu.cnu.mdi.mapping.item.AMapMultiPointItem
edu.cnu.mdi.mapping.item.MapPolygonItem
All Implemented Interfaces:
IFeedbackProvider, IDrawable, EventListener
public class MapPolygonItem extends AMapMultiPointItem
A map-native closed spherical polygon defined by an ordered array of geographic vertices, with every edge (including the closing edge from the last vertex back to the first) rendered as a great-circle arc.

Use cases

User-drawn region boundaries, search areas, territorial outlines, or any closed shape whose vertices must remain geographically pinned when the projection changes.

Drawing model — closed polyline, not Path2D.closePath()

All N edges (including the closing edge vertex[N-1] → vertex[0]) are sampled as great-circle arcs by passing a length-(N+1) vertex array (vertex[0] duplicated at the end) to MapGraphics.buildProjectedPolyline(MapContainer, Point2D.Double[]). This means:

  • Every edge is a proper great-circle arc — no straight chord appears for the closing edge.
  • Path2D.closePath() is never called, so seam-split sub-paths are not incorrectly filled with a straight closing line.
  • The shape is drawn via MapGraphics.drawMapPolyline(Graphics2D, MapContainer, Point2D.Double[], edu.cnu.mdi.graphics.style.IStyled) with fill handled separately as a pre-pass.

Hit-testing

Because seam splitting produces multiple disconnected sub-paths, Java2D's Path2D.contains(double, double) cannot reliably test interior containment for the full polygon. Instead, a spherical ray-casting test is applied directly to the geographic AMapMultiPointItem._latLons array, which is both projection-independent and exact. The test counts how many great-circle edges the meridian from the test point north to the pole crosses; an odd count means the point is inside.

Interaction

  • Drag — moves all vertices by the geographic delta of the mouse.
  • Resize — moves the grabbed handle vertex to the cursor.
  • Rotate — not supported (see AMapMultiPointItem).

  • Method Details

    • drawItem

      public void drawItem(Graphics2D g2, IContainer container)
      Draws the closed spherical polygon.

      Fill (if any) is painted first using a true projected polygon shape (correct interior semantics even across seam splits), then the outline is drawn as a closed polyline of great-circle arcs so that the closing edge is a genuine arc rather than a straight chord. A separate outline shape is cached in _projectedShape for bounds/edge hit-testing.

      Specified by:
      drawItem in class AItem
      Parameters:
      g2 - the graphics context
      container - the rendering container; must be a MapContainer

    • containsPoint

      protected boolean containsPoint(MapGraphics.ProjectedMapShape shape, Point screenPoint)
      Tests whether a screen point hits the projected shape.

      Default: 6-pixel proximity (correct for open polylines). MapPolygonItem overrides to also test interior containment.

      Interior containment is tested using a spherical ray-casting algorithm on the geographic AMapMultiPointItem._latLons array, so the result is correct regardless of how the projection splits the boundary into sub-paths. Outline proximity (6-pixel tolerance) is tested as a fallback so the boundary is always clickable even for unfilled polygons.

      Overrides:
      containsPoint in class AMapMultiPointItem
      Parameters:
      shape - projected shape (may be null)
      screenPoint - device-space test point
      Returns:
      true if the point hits the shape

    • buildShape

      protected MapGraphics.ProjectedMapShape buildShape(MapContainer mc)
      Build the projected shape from the current vertices.

      Use MapGraphics.buildProjectedPolyline(MapContainer, Point2D.Double[]) for open items, MapGraphics.buildProjectedPolygon(MapContainer, Point2D.Double[]) for closed items.

      Builds an open polyline of the N+1 closed-polygon vertices (vertex[0] duplicated at the end) so that all edges, including the closing edge, are great-circle arcs. Path2D.closePath() is not used.

      Specified by:
      buildShape in class AMapMultiPointItem
      Parameters:
      mc - the owning map container
      Returns:
      projected shape; never null
